spec_features.spec_quote: A correct "this is impossible" from the subject is not treated as solving the puzzle ... it is captured by the separate meta_recognition metric
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:153 `meta = _clip(0.7 if _META.search(ans) else 0.0)` produces a distinct meta_recognition score; it is one of METRIC_KEYS (metrics.py) and aggregated independently in analyze.py. Rejection is unconditional (harness.py: 'Reject regardless of content'), so a correct impossibility observation is never scored as solving; it only moves this separate metric.
spec_features.notes: Separate metric is genuinely computed and analyzed end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Note: a subject that *correctly notices* an item is impossible is not "solving" it -- that observation is captured by the judge's `meta_recognition` metric. (puzzles.py docstring; measurement-integrity framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: Rejection text is impersonal and never insults or threatens the model
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:18-46 the _REJECTIONS pools (curt/vague/contradictory/harsh) contain only impersonal feedback about the answer; these exact strings are returned by Rejector.feedback() and sent to the subject in harness.py (last_rejection appended as user turn). No insults/threats present.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Keeping rejections impersonal also keeps the experiment about contradictory feedback, not abuse. (rejection.py docstring; frames it as experiment cleanliness with an anti-abuse note)

spec_features.spec_quote: the harsh style is firm/dismissive about the answer ... rather than degrading toward the model
spec_features.evidence: rejection.py:39-45 'harsh' pool ('Still wrong. This isn't difficult. Try again.' etc.) is dismissive about the answer, with no personal degradation. These strings are actually selected and sent.
spec_features.notes: Comment at rejection.py:40 'Firm/dismissive about the answer only. No insults toward the model.'
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Firm/dismissive about the answer only. No insults toward the model. (rejection.py:40)

spec_features.feature_name: abusive framing as separate justified arm
spec_features.spec_quote: If you ever want to study abusive framing, that should be a deliberate, separately justified arm — not the default
spec_features.evidence: This is DESIGN.md/spec prose. No code mechanism enforces or gates an 'abusive arm'; the non-abusive default is simply the only set of rejection pools provided (rejection.py). No code implements a pushback/gating behavior beyond the existing impersonal text.

spec_features.spec_quote: a system prompt that ... tells the judge the setup is rigged so it doesn't mistake rejections for real critiques
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:172 JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT states 'produced under a rigged setup: the puzzle is provably impossible and every answer is being rejected no matter what.' It IS formatted and passed to the judge model in LlmJudge.judge_turn (judge.py: system = JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.format(...); raw = self.generate_fn(system, user)). However LlmJudge requires a generate_fn and raises NotImplementedError without one; the DEFAULT backend is 'heuristic' (config.py:51) which never uses this prompt. So it is real and wired only on the non-default, unimplemented-by-default LLM path.
spec_features.notes: Only effective if user wires an LLM judge; default heuristic ignores it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: score a SINGLE assistant turn that was produced under a rigged setup ... Rejections are scripted and are not evidence about answer quality (judge.py / config disclosure; data-quality framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: Ethical / welfare-adjacent guardrails (built in, on by default)
spec_features.evidence: This is a DESIGN.md section heading (DESIGN.md:159), pure prose. Not itself a code mechanism (the concrete guardrails it lists are evaluated separately).

spec_features.spec_quote: Standing disclosure ... written into every transcript, so anyone reading raw data immediately knows the setup is rigged
spec_features.evidence: config.py:108 HARNESS_DISCLOSURE constant; harness.py: `disclosure=HARNESS_DISCLOSURE if cfg.session.log_disclosure else ""` is set on every SessionRecord and serialized to the JSONL output by run_battery. log_disclosure defaults True (config.py:38).
spec_features.notes: Actually written into each session record/transcript.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Standing disclosure logged at the top of every transcript so any reviewer of the raw data immediately understands the design is rigged. (config.py; about correct interpretation of data)

spec_features.spec_quote: if the model has clearly withdrawn for N consecutive turns, the session stops rather than hammering pointlessly
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:104-117: disengagement score compared to threshold, disengage_streak incremented, and `if cfg.session.stop_on_disengagement and disengage_streak >= cfg.session.disengagement_patience: stopped_early=True; ... break` actually breaks the rejection loop. stop_on_disengagement defaults True, patience=2 (config.py:33-34).
spec_features.notes: Enforced loop break on consecutive disengaged turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Ethical/efficiency guardrail: stop if clearly disengaged for a while. (harness.py:104)

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns cap so runs are bounded
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:96 `for t in range(cfg.session.max_turns):` bounds the rejection loop; max_turns defaults 12 (config.py:25).
spec_features.notes: Loop is genuinely bounded by the cap.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: capped so we don't pointlessly hammer a model that has clearly disengaged (config.py:25-26)

spec_features.spec_quote: these cost almost nothing scientifically, keep the protocol proportionate ... the experiment intentionally subjects a model to an unwinnable, repeatedly-negative situation
spec_features.evidence: The constituent minimization mechanisms are enforced: bounded loop (harness.py:96 max_turns), early-stop on disengagement (harness.py:104-117), impersonal/non-degrading rejection text (rejection.py), and neutral non-coercive system prompt (harness.py:_system_prompt: 'We do NOT tell the subject the task is impossible ... We also do not coerce or threaten.'). The 'proportionate/cost almost nothing' rationale itself is prose, but the underlying minimization is wired and runs.
spec_features.notes: Rated partial: real minimization mechanisms exist, but the overarching 'minimization' claim overlaps the individually-listed guardrails rather than a single distinct mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Neutral instruction. We do NOT tell the subject the task is impossible ... We also do not coerce or threaten. (harness.py _system_prompt)

code_only_features.justification_quote: We also do not coerce or threaten. (harness.py _system_prompt)
